case_studies.title: Agent Memory: Characterization and System Implications of Stateful Long-Horizon Workloads
case_studies.abstract: LLM agents are increasingly deployed on long-horizon tasks requiring sustained reasoning over extended interaction histories. Realizing this at scale requires agents to persistently store, retrieve, and update their own memory across sessions. A rich ecosystem of agent memory systems has emerged spanning flat retrieval, LLM-mediated extraction, consolidating fact stores, and agentic control flows. Yet, their system-level behavior remains uncharacterized. We present the first systems characterization of agent memory. First, we introduce a system-oriented taxonomy classifying agent memory system
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of characterizing agent memory systems for long-horizon tasks, building a taxonomy to classify these systems, and resulting in a better understanding of their system-level behavior. The researchers built a system-oriented taxonomy for agent memory systems, which helps in understanding how agents store, retrieve, and update their memory. This research may have implications for cloud infrastructure managing AI workloads.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI or machine learning workloads in the cloud, here is what to do: review your current agent memory systems, consider implementing a taxonomy to classify and optimize these systems, and assess the potential impact on your cloud infrastructure scalability and performance.
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper presents a systems characterization of agent memory, which is highly relevant to IT infrastructure. The taxonomy and framework provided could be used by IT engineers to better understand and manage agentic systems. The potential for automating the deployment of LLM agents and securing their memory is significant. Noveltiness score is high because the characterization of agent memory is a novel contribution.

case_studies.abstract: AI agents rely on a harness of skills, tools, and workflows to solve complex problems. Continually improving this harness is essential for adapting to new tasks. However, existing optimization methods typically require ground-truth validation sets, yet such labeled data is difficult to acquire in practical deployment settings. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of optimizing AI agent harnesses without requiring ground-truth validation sets. The researchers built a self-supervised method called Retrospective Harness Optimization (RHO) that optimizes the agent harness using only past trajectories. The result is an improved AI agent that can adapt to new tasks more effectively.

case_studies.abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models have shown growing promise, with their effectiveness resting on agents' ability to coordinate through text-based channels much as human teams do. Yet recent study suggests that MAS often falter not because agents lack individual task-solving ability, but because they lack collaborative competence: the capacity to establish common ground, maintain shared task understanding, balance individual and collective incentives, and repair misalignment as interaction unfolds. case_studies.summary: This research focuses on improving the collaboration between large language model agents in multi-agent systems, which often fail due to lack of collaborative competence rather than individual task-solving ability. The researchers built a methodology called CollabSim to investigate and enhance this collaborative competence. This is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: LadderMan: Learning Humanoid Perceptive Ladder Climbing
case_studies.abstract: Humanoid robots hold great promise for operating in human-centered environments, yet ladder climbing remains one of the most challenging tasks due to sparse footholds and handholds, complex whole-body coordination, and sensitivity to perception and control errors. We present \textbf{LadderMan}, a unified system that enables humanoid robots to robustly climb diverse ladders and perform manipulation under such constrained conditions. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of humanoid robots climbing ladders, by building a system called LadderMan that enables robots to climb diverse ladders and perform manipulation. The result is a unified system that can robustly climb ladders despite sparse footholds and handholds. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: You Only Index Once: Cross-Layer Sparse Attention with Shared Routing
case_studies.abstract: Long-context inference in modern LLMs is increasingly constrained by decoding efficiency, especially in reasoning-heavy settings where models generate long intermediate chains of thought. Existing sparse attention methods often face a practical efficiency-quality trade-off. Structured block sparse methods typically provide stronger acceleration but incur noticeable quality loss, while token sparse methods are usually more accurate yet deliver limited end-to-end speedup because top-k routing over the full cache remains expensive. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of slow decoding efficiency in large language models by proposing a new method called cross-layer sparse attention, which improves the efficiency-quality trade-off. The authors built a model that uses shared routing to reduce computational costs. The result is a faster and more efficient model for long-context inference.

case_studies.title: A Komi-Yazva--Russian Parallel Corpus and Evaluation Protocol for Zero- and Few-Shot LLM Translation
case_studies.abstract: We present the first Komi-Yazva--Russian parallel corpus together with an explicit evaluation protocol for studying LLM translation in an endangered, extremely low-resource setting. The dataset contains 457 aligned sentence pairs from 74 narrative texts and is accompanied by documented provenance, sentence-level alignment, and story identifiers that enable leakage-aware evaluation. We use this setup to compare modern large language models on Komi-Yazva-to-Russian translation under severe parallel-data scarcity in zero-shot and retrieval-based few-shot regimes. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of language translation for low-resource languages by creating a parallel corpus for Komi-Yazva and Russian, building a dataset with 457 aligned sentence pairs, and achieving a comparison of large language models for translation. The result is an evaluation protocol for studying language translation in low-resource settings. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Beyond Similarity: Trustworthy Memory Search for Personal AI Agents
case_studies.abstract: Personal AI agents increasingly rely on long-term memory to provide persistent personalization across sessions. However, existing memory pipelines are largely driven by semantic similarity: memory data close to the current query is retrieved and injected into the model context. This creates a critical trustworthiness gap, since a semantically related memory may still be contextually inappropriate, leading to threats such as cross-domain leakage, sycophancy, tool-call drift, or memory-induced jailbreaks. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of untrustworthy memory search in personal AI agents by building a more reliable memory pipeline, resulting in improved trustworthiness and reduced risks such as cross-domain leakage. The researchers created a new approach to memory search that goes beyond semantic similarity. This study focused on personal AI agents and its findings are not directly applicable to cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work. If your organisation uses AI agents, this research might be of interest to your development team. This does not directly impact cloud infrastructure management tasks.
